corrected_value.title: When the Future Feels Worse than the Past: A Temporal Inconsistency in Moral Judgment.
corrected_value.title_o: When the future feels worse than the past: A temporal inconsistency in moral judgment.

decisions.quote:
We

conducted very close replications of three experiments derived from two influential TVA papers:

Studies 1 and 4 in Caruso et al. (2008), demonstrating TVA in monetary valuation, and Study 1

in Caruso (2010), demonstrating TVA in moral judgment.
decisions.location: Abstract, p. 2 (and Section 2.5, p. 10; References, p. 25)
decisions.reason: Experiment 2 directly re-tests Study 1 of Caruso (2010), 'When the Future Feels Worse than the Past: A Temporal Inconsistency in Moral Judgment', Journal of Experimental Psychology: General, 139(4), 610-624. Both shipped row 1271 and blind target_index 1 identify this exact same original study. The conflicting_dois pairing flag arose only because the replication paper's reference list (p. 25) printed a typographical/metadata error in the DOI (doi:10.1037/t33614-000, a PsycTESTS DOI) which the blind coder copied verbatim, whereas the shipped row records the actual JEP:General article DOI (10.1037/a0020757).

decisions.quote:
Second, we found no support for TVA in moral

judgments in our replication of Study 1 in Caruso (2010). Temporal location had little to no

effect on evaluations of fairness or negative feelings.
decisions.location: Section 4 (General Discussion), p. 19 (and Abstract, p. 2; Section 3.5, p. 18)
decisions.reason: The authors explicitly conclude that their direct replication of Study 1 in Caruso (2010) (Experiment 2) failed to find support for temporal value asymmetry in moral judgments, with null effects on both fairness judgments (p = .180, d = 0.13) and negative emotional intensity (p = .959, d = 0.01), summarized in Table 7 as 'No signal - inconsistent'. This outcome reflects the direct replication of Caruso (2010) Study 1 itself, independent of the conceptual extension.

decisions.location: Abstract, p. 2 (and Section 2.2, p. 8; Section 2.5, p. 10)
decisions.reason: The authors collected new experimental data from 423 Amazon MTurk participants to re-test the published findings of Study 1 in Caruso (2010) (as well as Studies 1 and 4 in Caruso et al., 2008), which meets the codebook definition of a replication.
